questions.question: Average of three numbers A, B, and C is 28 and average becomes 30 when value of D is also added. If average of A and B is 34, find the average of C and D.
questions.explanation:
Sum of A, B, and C = 28 × 3 = 84

Sum of A, B, C, and D = 30 × 4 = 120

Value of D = 120 - 84 = 36

Sum of A and B = 34 × 2 = 68

Value of C = 84 - 68 = 16

Sum of C and D = 36 + 16 = 52

Required average = \(\frac{52}{2}\)

= 26

questions.question: Average marks obtained by A, B and C in a Physics is 67 and average marks obtained by B, C and D in same subject is 73. If the sum of marks obtained by A and D is 158, then how many marks obtained by A?
questions.explanation:
Here, A + B + C = 3 × 67 = 201

B + C + D = 3 × 73 = 219

D - A = 219 - 201 = 18 => D = A + 18

A + D = 158 => D = 158 - A

Then, 158 - A = A + 18

A = 70

questions.question: The average marks of nine students in a group is 63. Three of them scored 78, 69 and 48 marks. What are the average marks of remaining six students?
questions.explanation: The average marks of remaining 6 students = \(\frac{\left( 9\  \times 63 \right) - \left( 78 + 69 + 48 \right)}{6}\) = 62

questions.question: The average age of P,Q, and R is 45. If the average age of P and Q is 40 years and that of Q and R 43 years. Find the age of Q.
questions.explanation:
Total age of P , Q and R = 45 \(\times\) 3 = 135

Total age of P + Q = 40 \(\times 2\) = 80

Total age of Q + R = 43\(\times\) 2 = 86

 ( P + Q) + (Q+R) - ( P+Q+R) = 80 + 86- 135

 Q = 31 years

questions.question: The average marks of class 10Th students is 35 and the number of students in class 10th is 30. The average marks of the first 18 students is 30 and the average marks of the last 11 students is 32. Then, find the marks of 19th students?
questions.explanation:
Average = \(\frac{\text{sum of all observation}}{\text{total number of observation}}\)

Sum of marks of 30 students = 30 x 35 = 1050

Sum of marks of first 18th students = 18 x 30 = 540

Sum of marks of last 11 students = 11 x 32 = 352

Marks obtained by 19th number students = 1050 – (540 + 352)

= 1050 – 892

= 158

questions.question: A, B, C and D are four consecutive odd numbers and their average is 64. What is the product of A and D?
questions.explanation:
Let (X = A) be an Odd integer

Then average = \(\frac{x + x + 2 + x + 4 + x + 6}{4} = 64\)

Or x = 61 = A and x + 6 = 67 = D

So, Product of A and D = 61 × 67 = 4087

questions.question: Five friends have an average weight of 64 kg. If Mohini is also included in the group, the average weight becomes 70 kg. What is Mohini's weight?
questions.explanation:
Total weight of five friend's =64×5=320 kg Total weight of

five friend's and Mohini's weight together =70×6=420 kg
Weight of Mohini =420-320=100 kg

questions.question: The average of runs of Rohit Sharma in 12 innings was 38.5 . He was to increase his average of runs by 5. How many runs must be made in his next innings?
questions.explanation:
New average of all the innings = 38.5 + 5 = 43.5 runs

Increase in runs = 12\(\times\) 5 = 60

Therefore, Required runs = 43.5 + 60 = 103.5

questions.question: The average temperature for Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday was 25 degrees and for Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday was 22 degrees. If the temperature on Monday was 20 degrees. Find the temperature on Friday?
questions.explanation:
Sum of temperature on monday, tuesday, wednesday, thursday = \(25 \times 4\  = \ 100\ degrees\)

Sum of temperature on tuesday, wednesday, thursday, friday

\(= \ 22 \times 4 = 88\ degrees\)

Monday’s temperature\(\  = \ 20\ degree\)

Therefore ; Friday temperature\(= \ 88 - (100 - 20) = \ 8\ degree\)

Option '8 degree' is the correct answer.

questions.question: The average score of a cricketer for 16 matches is 57 runs.If the average score for the first 8 matches is 34, then what is his average score for the last 8 matches.
questions.explanation:
Total score in 16 matches = 16 x 57

Total score of first 8 matches = 8 x 34

Hence, total score of last 8 matches = (16 x 57) - ( 8 x 34)

So, average of the last 8 matches will be = (16×57)- (8×34)8 = 80

questions.question: Three numbers are given. The average of first and third numbers is 8 more than that of second and third numbers. Find out the difference between the first and second numbers.
questions.explanation:
Let the numbers be \(a , b\), and \(c\) respectively.
\[
\begin{aligned}
& \therefore \frac{ a + c }{2}-\frac{ b + c }{2}=8 \\
& \Rightarrow( a + c )-( b + c )=8 \times 2=16 \\
& \Rightarrow a - b =16
\end{aligned}
\]

questions.question: The average weight of 19 boys was recorded as 64 kg. If the weight of the teacher was added, the average increased by 500 gm. What was the teacher's weight?
questions.explanation:
Average of the weight of 19 boys =64 kg
Sum of the weight of 19 boys =64×19=1216
Average of the weight of 19 boys and a teacher =64.5 kg
Sum of weight of 19 boys and a teacher =64.5×20=1290
Weight of teacher =1290-1216=74 kg

Total age of a class including teacher = (30 * 26.4) = 792 years

So, Age of teacher = (792 - 754) = 38 years.

questions.question: Meena buys 4 sarees at an average cost of Rs.1200 from a shop, If she buys 2 more sarees at an average cost of Rs.1500 from the same shop, what will be the average of all the sarees she buys in total?
questions.explanation:
Cost of 4 sarees = Rs 1200

Cost of 2 sarees = Rs 1500

By rule allegation;

Average of all the sarees, X\(\  = \frac{\ (1200 \times 4) + (1500 \times 2)}{4 + 2}\)

\(= \frac{7800}{6} = 1300\)

questions.question: The average height of the first six students is 170 cm, the average height of the last eight students is 175 cm. The average height of the total 16 students is 180 cm. Find the average height of the rest two students.
questions.explanation:
Sum of the heights of the first six students = 170 × 6 = 1020 cm
Sum of the heights of the last eight students = 175 × 8 = 1400 cm
Sum of the heights of the total 16 students = 180 × 16 = 2880
Sum of the height of the left 2 students = 2880 – 1020 – 1400 = 460

Average height of the left 2 students = \(\frac{460}{2}\) = 230 cm

questions.question: The average age of P,Q,R,S, and T is 50 years. The average age of P and Q is 45 years and the average age of R and S is 52 years. What will be the average age of T.
questions.explanation:
Total age of P,Q,R,S,T= 50× 5 = 250

Total age of P and Q =45 × 2 = 90

Total age of R and S = 52 × 2 =104

Therefore, the average age of T = 250 - (90 + 104)

= 56 years

questions.question: The average marks obtained by A, B and C are 48. The average marks obtained by B and C are 52. The ratio of marks obtained by A and C is 4:3. Find the marks obtained by B.
questions.explanation:
Total marks obtained by all three = 48×3 = 144

Total marks obtained by B and C = 52×2 = 104

Marks obtained by A = 144 −104 = 40

Marks obtained by C= 404×3=30

Marks obtained by B = 104-30 = 74

questions.question: The average weight of a class of 22 students is 40 kg. When the weight of the teacher is also included, the average weight increases by 750 gm. What is the weight of the teacher?
questions.explanation:
The total weight of 22 students = 40×22 = 880 kg

New average weight = 40 + 0.75 = 40.75 kg

Total weight of 22 students and teacher together = 23 × 40.75 = 937.25

Weight of teacher = 937.25 – 880 = 57.25 kg

questions.question: In a primary school 96 students are studying. Their average weight is \(30 \mathrm{~kg}\). If a student shift to another school the average weight is increased by \(200 \mathrm{gm}\). Find the weight of the student who shifted from the school.
questions.explanation:
Number of students \(=96\)
Average weight \(=30 \mathrm{~kg}\).
1 student leave the school then average weight is increased by \(200 \mathrm{gm}\).
Weight of student who shift from the school \(=\) Original average weight \(-(\) No of persons (Excluding the left out person) \(\times\) increase in average weight)
\[
\begin{aligned}
& =30-((96-1) \times 200 / 1000) \\
& \Rightarrow 30-(95 \times 1 / 5) \\
& \Rightarrow 30-19 \\
& \Rightarrow 11 \mathrm{~kg} .
\end{aligned}
\]
A Weight of the student who shifted from the school is \(11 \mathrm{~kg}\).
